newsitem.title: USA: Whitman sees Q2 EPS $0.05-$0.07 below yr-ago.
newsitem.headline: Whitman sees Q2 EPS $0.05-$0.07 below yr-ago.

text.p: Whitman Corp said Monday it expects its earnings for the second quarter will be $0.05 to $0.07 a share below the $0.39 a share earned in the year-ago second quarter.

Whitman said results from its Pepsi-Cola General Bottlers, the world's largest independent Pepsi-Cola franchise, were hurt by unusually competitive pricing and unseasonably cold weather, as well as a $3.0 million charge for staff reduction.
Its Midas International franchised automotive service unit was hurt by softness in consumer demand for automotive repair and a less favorable mix of products and services.

"Despite the issues affecting our second quarter results, we feel good about the long-term prospects for our companies," Chelberg said. "Each is best in class in its industry. We have high expectations for them going forward."
Earlier, Whitman said it plans to spin off its Hussmann Corp and Midas International businesses to shareholders.
Hussmann is the world's largest supplier of refrigeration systems for the food industry, with sales of more than $1.0 billion in 1996.
Midas has more than 2,500 stores in 17 countries. Worldwide retail sales by Midas dealers were more than $1.3 billion in 1996.
Whitman's Pepsi-Cola General Bottlers represents about 12 percent of Pepsi-Cola's volume in the United States. It also distributes Pepsi-Cola products in markets in Poland, Russia and the Baltics.
